sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Small Parcel Sorting and Direct-Injection Linehaul

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (FTA/TPA), in force 2012
Panama–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty, in force 1999; Panama–UK Double Taxation Agreement, in force 2021
Panama–Netherlands Bilateral Investment Treaty, in force 2001
Panama–Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty, in force 1998
Panama–Mexico Bilateral Investment Treaty, in force 2004
Panama–Germany Bilateral Investment Treaty, in force 1990

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT and Countering Proliferation Financing Measures), as amended by Law 129 of 2020 and Law 2 of 2022; Executive Decree 363 of 2015 (implementing regulation); Law 70 of 2019 (establishing the Beneficial Owners Registry / Registro de Beneficiarios Finales), implemented by Executive Decree 149 of 2020; Law 21 of 2017 (Register of Holders of Legal Persons); Cabinet Decree 274 of 2020 (FIU consolidated rulebook and sanctions coordination).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each Founder and Foundation Council member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin-country notary public or competent passport authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police Clearance Certificate (certificado de antecedentes penales) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal-records authority of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing solvency and source of the founding contribution
Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the Panamanian registered agent to file the foundation
Certificate of Good Standing, existence, and incumbency of the corporate Founder (if any)
Address verification documentation (utility invoice or bank statement issued within six months) for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility company or financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation (traducción jurada) of all apostilled documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Sworn Public Translator (traductor público autorizado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal notarization; no fresh apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the Founder, Foundation Council (Consejo de Fundación), protectors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against (i) domestic Politically Exposed Persons lists maintained under Law 23 of 2015; (ii) OFAC SDN List; (iii) UN Consolidated Sanctions List; and (iv) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions, supplemented by Panama FIU risk alerts. Enhanced due diligence is compulsory for any individual holding or ultimately controlling 25% or more of foundation rights, for PEPs, and for counterparties domiciled in jurisdictions flagged by FATF. Screening evidence must be preserved in the resident agent's client dossier for at least five years after termination of the professional relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Digital Name Search, Clearance and Reservation System (Búsqueda y Reserva de Nombre / Certificado de Búsqueda)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be legible in Spanish/Latin script; a foreign-language denomination is permitted only with a Spanish-language rendering for registry indexing, and the name must contain or be directly accompanied by the operative token 'Fundación' or 'Foundation'. Names identical, phonetically equivalent, or bearing high visual similarity to any existing registered legal person are refused; denominations implying governmental patronage, regulated financial activity, or misleading public purpose require prior institutional clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five (5) business days of the adverse name decision, the applicant or its registered agent must file a written motion for reconsideration (recurso de revocatoria) before the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá. A denial of that motion may be contested within five (5) further days through a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Administrative Tribunal pursuant to Law 38 of 2000. A parallel administrative remedy is to re-submit a visually and phonetically distinct alternative foundation name under a fresh 30-day reservation certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office accommodation is permissible solely for day-to-day commercial back-office administration of the parcel consolidation hub; it cannot replace the statutory registered office situated at the licensed resident agent's physical Panamanian premises. The resident agent (agente residente) must remain physically present, receive official service of process, and maintain the foundation's statutory records, satisfying the substance requirements of Law 18 of 2010 and Law 23 of 2015.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months for a Low_Risk_Standard ISIC 5229 parcel consolidation entity, rising to 20% if throughput from PEP-flagged or sanctions-listed counterparty jurisdictions exceeds 25% of consolidated volume. FIU-ordered unannounced inspections are lawful under Law 23 of 2015 and Cabinet Decree 274 of 2020.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search, clearance certificate (certificado de búsqueda), and reservation fee
Notarization and protocolización (legalization) of the Spanish-language Foundation Charter (carta fundacional) and internal reglamento
Government inscription (inscripción) of the Private Interest Foundation with the Public Registry
Legal drafting of the Foundation Charter, by-laws, foundation purpose clauses, and confidential provisions (cláusulas secretas)
AML/CFT customer due diligence, UBO identification, PEP and sanctions screening, and creation of the internal compliance dossier (expediente conozca su cliente)
Initial filing in the Beneficial Owners Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent (agente residente) and statutory registered office service, first annual period
Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of founder passports, police certificates, bank references, and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of origin country / Panama Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Consular Section)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation (traducción jurada al español) of all founder and UBO international documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn Public Translator (traductor público autorizado), Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUC (tax identification number) registration and aviso de operación business activity notification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de julio de 1995 (Régimen de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Ley No. 8 de 2015; Articles 1, 3, 4, 6, 10, 13 and 18; supplemented by the Regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter) executed as a private instrument or public deed and submitted through a licensed resident agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required; the Foundation must receive an initial patrimony or endowment of any nominal value, customarily not less than US$1. No escrow deposit or paid-in capital account is required before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE INITIAL COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME] PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION: The initial Council, acting under the Foundation Charter and Law 25 of 1995, resolves: (1) to accept the founder's endowment and initial patrimony of [US$ amount]; (2) to adopt [registered address], Panama, as the registered office and to ratify [resident agent name] as Resident Agent; (3) to appoint [name] and [name] as Council members, [name] as President, and [name] as Secretary/Treasurer, with full powers for banking, contracts and governance; (4) to approve the Foundation Charter and direct the Resident Agent to submit all registration documents to the Public Registry. This resolution is effective immediately. Dated [date]. Signed by the Council.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registros, online consultation window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search to verify that the proposed foundation name is not already registered or too similar to another legal entity. The name must include 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' and may be reserved for a limited period after clearance.
required_dossiers: Copy of founder's passport or national ID
Power of attorney if acting through a resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, immediately submit an alternative name and pay no additional penalty; a fresh reservation is issued on the cleared name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian notary public or licensed resident agent with notarization capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Acta Constitutiva in Spanish stating the foundation name, purpose, registered office, endowment, council members, beneficiaries and rules for amendment or dissolution. Execute the instrument with notarized signatures and ensure the founder declares the contributed assets.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any notarial or content deficiency identified by counsel and re-execute the instrument before a notary; the corrected document supersedes the defective version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of resident agent and adoption of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed resident agent in Panama (law firm or corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a resident agency agreement with a licensed Panama lawyer or agent who will maintain the registered office and statutory records at a physical address in Panama and act as the service-of-process point. The agent performs customer due diligence before issuance of the acceptance certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident agent refuses engagement due to incomplete KYC, supply the required identification, source of funds, and ownership information within the requested due diligence period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of government registration fees and stamp taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Treasury unit and online payment portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the state incorporation fee of approximately USD 250 plus applicable stamp taxes through the resident agent or the Registry's payment portal. Obtain the official payment receipt to be appended to the final filing package.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fee receipt contains errors, obtain a corrected receipt through the Treasury unit or portal by reconciling underpayment or overpayment before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to the Public Registry for inscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Foundation Charter, resident agent acceptance, name reservation, KYC documents and fee receipt with the Registry. Upon successful review and inscription, the Foundation acquires separate legal personality and receives a registered certificate.
required_dossiers: Resident agent consent and acceptance certificate
Original or certified power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a reparo or query, address the stated objection within the statutory cure period by amending the charter or providing supplementary documentation; any re-filing fee must be paid promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipio de Panamá for Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Foundation's Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) from DGI and, if the foundation or its operating entity maintains physical premises for the parcel consolidation hub, file the municipal Aviso de Operación. Where commercial activity is intended, the applicable operating entity must hold the RUC and business license in its own name.
required_dossiers: Lease or title for the physical premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality disputes the classification of activities, file an application for clarification or amend the Aviso de Operación to accurately reflect passive asset holding and logistics operations conducted through a separate operating entity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas; Municipio de Panamá – Dirección General de Rentas Municipales for municipal business and operational licenses
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Permiso Municipal de Funcionamiento for a parcel consolidation and distribution warehouse

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección General de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I or II under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 14 de agosto de 2009; a small parcel consolidation hub generally requires a Category I Diagnóstico Ambiental, while larger facilities with relevant floor area or throughput require a Category II Estudio de Impacto Ambiental (EsIA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The facility must comply with MiAMBIENTE technical norms: no untreated process wastewater discharge; if treated and discharged, pH 6–9, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 150 mg/L and TSS ≤ 50 mg/L unless stricter site-specific limits apply. VOC emissions from packaging and vehicle operations must be controlled to applicable ambient air standards; packaging waste and solid waste must be stored separately and transferred only to authorized waste handlers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire safety and prevention certification; municipal or Ministry of Public Works structural load inspection for warehouse racking and mezzanines; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) workplace hygiene and occupational safety review; and Instituto Nacional de Seguros (INS) employer registration for workers' compensation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; official e-filing and registration portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa); public information portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) PIF must first be constituted by notarized 'Acta Constitutiva' and registered with the Registro Público de Panamá, with mandatory appointment of a Resident Agent (abogado/attorney). 2) The Resident Agent files the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) application with the DGI via the Sede Electrónica, attaching the foundation charter, Public Registry certificate, and ID of the Resident Agent and beneficiaries/founders where required. 3) Obtain the Firma Electrónica (digital certificate) issued through the Registro Público for the tax administrator/representative. 4) DGI assigns the RUC and a CIIU economic-activity code; the PIF is registered as an 'Obligado Tributario' and, if it performs taxable supplies within Panama, is simultaneously enrolled for ITBMS. 5) A foreign-operated PIF must designate a local fiscal representative or maintain the Resident Agent as contact point for tax notices; non-resident entities with no Panamanian-source activity are generally not required to obtain a RUC. 6) RUC updates for changes in officers, address, or economic activities must be filed within 15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch entity elections. The PIF is a separate juridical person taxed at foundation/entity level on Panama-source income only (territorial taxation), while foreign-source income is exempt under Law 25 of 1995 and Article 694 of the Código Fiscal. The foundation deed may elect between: (a) strictly private wealth-administration activities (full exemption for non-Panama income; B/.300 annual foundation tax payable to the Public Registry); or (b) engaging in commercial business within Panama, which triggers RUC/ITBMS and full taxation of Panamanian-source income at the 25% corporate rate. No other elective classification is available; source characterization follows the situs rules of the Código Fiscal.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0.00 - no annual-turnover de minimis threshold; ITBMS registration is mandatory for any person habitually transferring goods or rendering services whose economic effect is situated in Panama. An optional simplified small-taxpayer regime (trimestral) applies to persons with annual taxable turnover not exceeding B/.36,000 (USD 36,000).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing ('Facturación Electrónica / eFactura') under Law 159 of 2020 and DGI regulations, implemented through the DGI's Sede Electrónica e-invoicing module. Each invoice must be structured in the official XML schema, digitally signed with a valid Firma Electrónica, and transmitted to the DGI fiscal web service for real-time authorization ('acuse') before delivery to the buyer; the system assigns an electronic invoice number and a machine-readable QR/stamping element. The regime is compulsory for Gran Contribuyente (large taxpayers) and is being phased to all obligated taxpayers; legacy DGI-authorized bound invoices (facturas físicas) and fiscal cash-register printers are being phased out concurrently. Foreign-service providers rendering offshore services without Panamanian nexus are generally outside the e-invoicing mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) applies to: (i) physical export of goods from Panama to abroad, evidenced by the customs export declaration; (ii) services rendered in Panama for use, consumption, or exploitation outside Panama, including cross-border freight forwarding, parcel consolidation, sorting, and direct-injection linehaul services performed for non-resident e-commerce merchants; (iii) supplies made within Colon Free Zone (Zona Libre de Colón), Panama Pacifico and other authorized special economic zones; and (iv) services rendered to non-residents when the direct benefit and use of the service occurs outside Panama. The exporter/renderer must separately show the 0% rate on the invoice and retain input-ITBMS credits; where input tax exceeds output tax on zero-rated exports, the taxpayer files the monthly ITBMS declaration and may claim an input VAT refund ('Devolución de crédito fiscal') through the DGI. The DGI may approve the refund only upon documentary verification of the export and receipt of foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Declaración Única Aduanera) duly accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) with exit confirmation (regularization of 'salida' within statutory deadlines)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing actual movement from Panamanian territory
International commercial invoice (export pre-factura/factura) reflecting 0% ITBMS and accurate HS codes
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / bank credit advice proving receipt of foreign currency
Packing list and, where applicable, warehouse-receipt or consolidation manifest evidencing the parcel-sorting scope
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits zero-rated export claims by cross-matching DUA exit records, B/L manifests, and the taxpayer's banking evidence, and may reclassify non-substantiated receivables as Panama-source income taxable at 25% ISR plus 7% ITBMS, interest, and punitive multipliers. Misrepresenting domestic deliveries as exports is tax fraud under Código Fiscal Article 762, subject to fines of 100% to 200% of evaded tax, retrospective clawback of the 0% rate and input-VAT refunds, suspension of the RUC, and criminal sanctions for willful false declarations. Refund claims wrongly obtained expose the taxpayer to restitution, surcharges, and personal/legal-representative liability. Repatriation of export proceeds later than 180 days is a documented audit trigger and increases the risk of source recharacterization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No de jure central bank. Panama is a fully dollarized economy; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the bank and finance-sector regulator, while Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent, clearing house, and government treasury bank. The Monetary and Financial Board (Junta Monetaria) sets only advisory monetary parameters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama uses the USD as legal tender and the Balboa is a 1:1 accounting unit with no physical circulation. There are no exchange-control restrictions on capital or current account transactions. Profit remittances from a Private Interest Foundation operating in Panama are not subject to exchange approval; only a 10% dividend/remittance tax applies if the underlying income was sourced in Panama, and no prior FX authorization or exit permit is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama does not require export receivables to be surrendered, converted, or repatriated within any statutory timeline. Proceeds may be held in USD or any freely convertible currency in the foundation's operational bank accounts, subject only to standard transaction reporting thresholds under SBP AML rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational clearing account (ACH Panama participant / fiscal agent)
Capital escrow account and operational corporate account
Capital escrow account and operational corporate account
Capital escrow account / Private Interest Foundation treasury account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate to High as an ancillary rail only. Panama's SBP regulatory sandbox and the new fintech law allow for licensed local electronic payment institutions, but offshore digital EMIs (including Airwallex, Wise, Payoneer) may hold USD funds and route settlement for cross-border parcel disbursements. They are not acceptable as a primary treasury account for a Panamanian PIF because SBP-supervised banks require a local licensed account for capital escrow, dividend distributions, and audited balance-sheet evidence. EMIs are legally usable for supplier payouts, marketplaces remittance, and sub-ledger minorexpense clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the first account opening. Tier-1 Panamanian banks expect at least one founding council member, the judicial agent, or an authorized attorney-in-fact to appear in person for the KYC interview in Panama. Remote opening is possible for existing institutionally vetted non-resident clients if the full dossier is notarized, apostilled, and supported by a live videoconference interview; however, the Public Registry certified foundation deed and the final beneficial owner register must be filed physically or via a licensed Panamanian counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation flagged as a complex or opaque trust-like vehicle by the bank's underwriting engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Package containing: (1) certified Public Registry extract and foundation charter/bylaws; (2) legal opinion from a Panamanian lawyer explaining PIF as a separate liability vehicle with no trust relationship; (3) list of foundation council members; (4) original or apostilled foundation resolutions appointing the authorized signatories; (5) commercial contracts proving the active e-commerce parcel consolidation business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the initial capital escrow injection cannot be verified from origin.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide at least 12 months of source-account bank statements for each contributor, a source-of-wealth statement with supporting transaction history, audited or unaudited financial statements of the ultimate parent, signed declaration of funding structure, and evidence of the commercial purpose (warehouse lease, parcel facility agreements, cargo insurance policies, cross-border e-commerce marketplace contracts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership structure appears layered or unclear because PIF is a foundation without shares.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a certified final beneficial ownership register filed with the Panamanian beneficial ownership registry, a written ownership/beneficiary chart up to natural persons with supporting ID and PEP status, foundation council resolutions affirming the beneficiary class, and a sworn statement of non-tolerance of bearer instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction patterns include regional jurisdictions with elevated sanctions/AML risk (e.g., counterparties in CN, HK, or Free Zone customers).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Build a counterparty due-diligence file containing: (1) trade invoices and packing lists; (2) customs declarations (SIGA/PIMA or Esik) for each parcel-consolidation shipment; (3) bills of lading and direct-injection linehaul contracts; (4) OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening results; (5) counterparty KYB questionnaires with beneficial owner information; (6) transaction flow diagrams linking each payment to the underlying logistics service.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 from the parent or contributor to the PIF's USD account maintained at a tier-1 Panamanian bank (Banco General or Banco Nacional de Panamá). Payment must reference 'Capital Contribution' or 'Intra-Company Loan to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF' and include a transaction purpose code consistent with SBP classification (e.g., corporate treasury contribution). The bank will verify the source of funds and record the credit to the capital escrow account; no exchange-control permission is required. Required verification documents include the foundation resolution approving the contribution, the capital plan, and a source-of-wealth dossier for each inbound leg.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the parcel-consolidation hub are executed through (1) SWIFT MT103 for international supplier payments, freight forwarders, and linehaul operators; (2) commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) issued by Banco General or Banistmo for high-value shipments and inventory prepayment; (3) ACH Panama (Cámara de Compensación Nacional) for local operational expenses, utility payments, customs brokerage, and payroll; and (4) digital EMI rails such as Airwallex and local clearing for last-mile supplier reimbursement in USD and selected regional currencies. All disbursements may be settled in USD without FX conversion, preserving liquidity and reducing spread risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/PAB non-deliverable forwards (economically redundant due to the fixed 1:1 currency board system)
Offshore or internationally licensed deliverable FX forwards on CNY, EUR, MXN, and BRL against USD for supplier payment hedging
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY, EUR, and other controlled regional currencies for matched parcel linehaul exposures
Cross-currency basis swaps (USD vs EUR, MXN, and BRL) executed with tier-1 international correspondents to match freight and e-commerce settlement flows
Simple FX spot transactions through SBP-regulated Panamanian banks or their global custodians

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Tasa Única Anual) for Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge plus monthly interest; no issuance of tax clearance (Paz y Salvo); registry cancellation or strike-off after three consecutive unpaid years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada Anual ISR) covering Panamanian-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of 25% of the tax due plus monthly delinquency interest; enforcement and registration restrictions until the return is accepted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business License Renewal (Aviso de Operación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipio de Panamá, Dirección de Rentas Municipales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal fines, penalty interest on unpaid fees, and closure of the local operating premises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Owner Reconfirmation and UBO Data Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On each annual anniversary and within 30 days after any beneficial-ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to USD 10,000 for false or omitted beneficial-owner data and suspension of registry filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is required when annual Panamanian-source gross revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 5,000,000; below these thresholds the foundation must still prepare financial statements and present a signed accountant's report with the ISR return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for entities without public accountability that are below the Panamanian audit threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The foundation council and registered agent must obtain annual written confirmation from all founders, council members, and significant beneficiaries; any change in the actual economic exerciser must be reported to DGI within 30 calendar days. The PIF has no share register; control is recorded through foundation charter, council appointments, and beneficiary designations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Protector Appointments
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax: only Panama-source income is taxed. Foreign-source income of a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is exempt. No general tax holiday applies. The PIF may be subject to the annual B/.300.00 franchise tax and, if active in Panama, to local municipal patent/trade-license taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 (IR-101) - Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas / Legal Entity Income Tax Return; filed electronically via the Panama DGI online platform (SITIO / e-Tax 2.0).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance income tax payments are required for taxpayers whose prior-year taxable income exceeds USD 50,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (for a 31 December year-end, the statutory filing deadline is 31 March of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered taxpayer identification number of the PIF (RUC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must be registered in Panama and possess a valid RUC; a non-resident owned PIF must still obtain Panamanian fiscal documentation before filing.
If the PIF uses a non-calendar fiscal year, the return must reflect the approved distinct accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3: Ingresos de fuente panameña (Panama-source gross income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from services rendered or assets located in Panama, including parcel consolidation, sorting, linehaul and related logistics services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no physical sorting, consolidation or linehaul activity occurs in Panama, enter zero; document this with contracts, route manifests and geolocation records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4: Ingresos de fuente extranjera (Exempt foreign-source income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from services performed or assets used outside Panama, excluded from territorial taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide clear attribution of cross-border e-commerce logistical revenue to foreign contracts; reconcile with Airwallex and local clearing settlement statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and expenses directly connected to Panama-source gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not allocate costs or overheads to exempt foreign-source income; maintain full supporting invoices and transfer pricing contemporaneous documentation.
Compute in US dollars/Balboas at the official exchange rate; a zero or negative amount results in no tax due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 25% statutory corporate tax rate on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panama-source income is declared, enter zero and attach a sworn statement of territorial scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8: Créditos y pagos a cuenta (Credits and advance payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly ISR advance payments, DTA withholding credits, and other eligible credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach certificates of credits and evidence of foreign tax credits only if treaty relief applies; excess credits may be refunded after audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of a month of delay, up to a maximum of 50%; late payment interest of 1.5% per month (simple) is added. Intentional non-filing may also trigger criminal tax proceedings and personal liability for directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends or distributions from Panama-source profits of a Panamanian legal entity or foundation constituted as a business; distributions from a PIF funded exclusively with foreign-source assets are outside Panama territorial taxation and not subject to dividend WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama applies DTA relief upon: (1) obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence; (2) submitting Form 101-R or the relevant DGI relief request form before the distribution is made; (3) providing evidence of beneficial ownership, the foundation charter, and economic substance status of the PIF; and (4) awaiting DGI certification of the reduced WHT rate before implementing the payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for the use of intangibles in Panama: statutory WHT rate 12.5% on gross amount, reducible under an applicable DTA. Interest paid to non-resident lenders for loans used wholly outside Panama: 0% Panama withholding; interest with Panama-source usage: statutory 12.5% WHT, subject to any LOB/treaty limitations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when annual Panama-source gross income exceeds B/.3,000,000 (USD 3,000,000); Master File mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated global revenue exceeds USD 15,000,000; Country-by-Country Report mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue above USD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2021 and Decree 259 of 2022) apply to PIFs conducting relevant activities, including parcel distribution/consolidation, headquarters, logistics and service functions. The PIF must demonstrate direction and management in Panama, maintain adequate fixed premises and local employees, and file an annual economic substance report with the DGI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Non-Filing of Panama-Source Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an active parcel consolidation and linehaul hub in Panama while causing the PIF to omit Panama-source income on Form 101, misclassifying domestic sorting revenues as foreign-source, or conducting business through the foundation without a RUC or tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge of up to 200%-300% of tax evaded; civil penalty of 25% of the omitted tax; criminal fine of B/.5,000 to B/.100,000; imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director and Foundation Council members can be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid Panama-source taxes; personal passport/travel bans may be imposed; criminal convictions can result in imprisonment for directors who knowingly sign fraudulent returns.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF as a hollow invoice-mill with no physical sorting facility, no Panamanian employees, no board meetings or decisions made in Panama, while claiming the exemption for foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic substance penalty of up to B/.250,000 for false or missing substance declarations; annulment of tax exemption benefits; possible strike-off of the foundation by the DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors face civil liability for the fines and any resulting tax reassessment; the corporate veil may be pierced where the foundation is found to be an instrumentality of the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Abusive Related-Party Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-arm's-length consolidated parcel-handling fees to group companies, routing e-commerce payments through the PIF, and failing to prepare or submit local file/master file documentation upon exceeding the statutory threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compensatory tax adjustment plus penalty of up to 15% of the omitted tax attributable to the TP adjustment; non-deductibility of undocumented transactions; administrative fines for non-filing of TP declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve intercompany arrangements without TP documentation become personally liable for the adjusted corporate tax and penalties; travel bans can be issued pending payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an opaque PIF to conceal beneficial owners while operating an e-commerce parcel hub, accepting funds from unverified consignors through Airwallex/local clearing rails and failing to file beneficial ownership information with the Panamanian Financial Analysis Unit (UAF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties for AML violations up to B/.500,000; criminal penalties for money laundering from 5 to 10 years' imprisonment; forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers, directors and foundation protectors may be personally indicted; civil asset seizure and travel bans apply; corporate veil piercing is permitted under Panama's AML statutes.
